tasks.title: Lecture #41
tasks.instruction: Listen to part of a psychology podcast.
tasks.transcript: My brother Alex has always wanted to get a cat. He likes cats better than dogs. One day he sent me an online article titled Which Pet is Right for You and says see, even experts agree cats are better. But when I read the article, nowhere did it say that. The article presents balanced facts. Dogs are loyal and trainable while cats are independent and low maintenance. My brother was not being dishonest, he simply focused only on the parts that preys cats and skimmed over or dismissed the parts that highlight dogs advantages. This is called confirmation bias. Our brains are lazy. They like consistency. Information that aligns with what we already know is easier to understand and less mentally taxing. So our brains seek it out and filter out the rest. This affects the decisions we make in our daily life as well as in work. Scientists are not immune to confirmation bias. Researchers may unintentionally design experiments or interpret data in ways that support their hypotheses, overlooking results that do not fit their expectations. Flawed conclusions in scientific studies can lead to serious consequences. So what can we do to minimize confirmation bias? The first step is to recognize the existence of confirmation bias. Know that you might be biased. Then actively seek out information that challenges your beliefs. Don't only talk with people who hold the same views as yours and slow down. Don't make hasty decisions.

questions.stem: What is the talk mainly about?

options.A: What confirmation bias is and ways to reduce its effect
options.B: What makes certain individuals more vulnerable to confirmation bias than others
options.C: How scientists discovered the phenomenon of confirmation bias
options.D: How everyday decision making differs from scientific decision making

questions.analysis: 答案：A 题目问的是：讲座主要内容是什么？ 定位原文：This is called confirmation bias… what can we do to minimize… 选项分析： A. 解释确认偏误及减少方法。完整概括，因此正确。 B. 哪些人更容易受影响。未重点讨论。 C. 如何被发现。未提及。 D. 日常 vs 科学对比。只是部分内容。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about the viewpoint expressed in the article his brother sent him?

options.A: Its author has a strong preference for cats over dogs.
options.C: Its viewpoint is an example of confirmation bias.
options.D: Its author has a slight preference for dogs over cats.

questions.analysis: 答案：B 题目问的是：文章观点如何？ 定位原文：The article presents balanced facts. 选项分析： A. 偏向猫。错误。 B. 平衡观点。直接对应，因此正确。 C. 是 confirmation bias。错误，是他哥哥的问题。 D. 偏向狗。错误。

questions.stem: What does the speaker mean when he says that the human brain is lazy?

options.A: The human brain needs to take frequent rests.
options.B: The human brain tends to forget new information very quickly.
options.C: The human brain tends to focus only on information that fits existing beliefs.
options.D: The human brain gets easily bored from lack of new stimuli.

questions.analysis: 答案：C 题目问的是：大脑“懒惰”是什么意思？ 定位原文：brains seek information that aligns… filter out the rest 选项分析： A. 需要休息。未提及。 B. 容易忘。未提及。 C. 只关注符合已有观点的信息。直接对应，因此正确。 D. 容易无聊。未提及。

questions.stem: What does the speaker point out about scientists?

options.A: They have done a lot of research on what causes confirmation bias.
options.B: They experience confirmation bias while conducting research.
options.C: They believe it is possible to completely overcome confirmation bias.
options.D: They are better at making unbiased decisions than other people are.

questions.analysis: 答案：B 题目问的是：科学家有什么特点？ 定位原文：Scientists are not immune… may unintentionally design… 选项分析： A. 研究很多。不是重点。 B. 也会有确认偏误。直接对应，因此正确。 C. 可以完全避免。错误。 D. 更客观。相反。
